ai.title: Switch diff retry to o3-mini
ai.summary: Diff block retry logic now uses o3-mini via promptOpenAI, replacing the previous Sonnet and DeepSeek routing. This change simplifies backend model selection by removing conditional cost-mode branching in generate-diffs-prompt.ts. A new getMessageText utility in util/messages.ts extracts plain text from message content, enabling process-file-block.ts to pass lastUserPrompt to the retry handler. The refactor touches backend/src/generate-diffs-prompt.ts, main-prompt.ts, process-file-block.ts, and util/messages.ts.

eli5.text: When the assistant makes an edit using a search-and-replace block and that exact text doesn't match anything in the file, it retries the edit by sending the request to a new model. Previously these retry requests could be routed to one of several different models depending on a cost setting, which sometimes routed a retry to a slower or less reliable model; now they always go to the same model so retries are consistent. This only affects files whose edits fail to match, so most users won't notice anything different unless they were hitting retry failures before. The change is live today as part of the backend's edit-correction flow.

ai.title: Hard filter knowledge.md in request-files-prompt
ai.summary: getExampleFileList now filters out paths containing knowledge.md before random selection. Prompt instructions tightened to explicitly forbid including these files in LLM responses. Applies to both standard and key-file request modes in backend/src/find-files/request-files-prompt.ts. Prevents knowledge files from leaking into example file lists sent to the model.

eli5.text: When the system picks example files to show the assistant, it now skips any file containing 'knowledge.md' so those files can't leak into what gets sent to the model. The written instructions telling the assistant to exclude those files were also made stricter. This affects internal file selection and prompt guidance used during backend processing. You wouldn't notice this directly, but it ensures sensitive knowledge files stay out of example file lists sent to the model.

ai.title: Record cost for relace requests
ai.summary: Added fixed cost tracking for `relace-fast-apply` model. `message-cost-tracker.ts` defines `RELACE_FAST_APPLY_COST` and short-circuits `calcCost` for this model. `relace-api.ts` now constructs a synthetic `fakeRequestContent` using `createMarkdownFileBlock` and passes it as the `request` payload to `saveMessage`, replacing the previous empty array. Scope: backend billing and relace API integration.

eli5.text: The system now charges a fixed one-cent fee for each relace-fast-apply request, regardless of how long the request or response is. This affects billing tracking for that specific model. If you looked, you'd see the request content recorded includes the initial code and edit snippet formatted together, rather than an empty field.

ai.title: Trim new-files prompt guidance
ai.summary: Removed lean-towards-YES bias from new-files check prompt in backend/src/find-files/check-new-files-necessary.ts. Collapsed multi-line logger.error call to single line. Internal change to AI agent file-reading decision logic.

eli5.text: The instructions guiding the assistant's decision to read new files no longer gently nudge it toward reading them when uncertain; instead, the assistant will choose not to read new files more often in borderline cases. This is a behind-the-scenes adjustment to the assistant's internal file-reading logic, so you wouldn't notice any visible change in the interface, but the assistant may skip opening files it isn't confident are strictly necessary. Live today.

ai.title: Tweak terminal tool use prompt in main-prompt.ts
ai.summary: Simplified terminal tool use instructions in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. Removed conditional logic requiring further instruction fulfillment after writing `STOP_MARKER`. Directive now strictly mandates `STOP_MARKER` output upon terminal command success and request completion.

eli5.text: You now get a cleaner signal about when the assistant has finished acting on your behalf. Previously, after the assistant ran a successful command that completed your request, a reminder would still ask it to pause and wait for your further instructions. That reminder is gone: on your screen, after a completed request, the assistant simply stops with the agreed-upon end marker instead of offering to keep listening. It is a small behind-the-scenes tweak to the instruction prompt, live today.

ai.title: Refine new file reading prompt logic
ai.summary: Updated the prompt in backend/src/find-files/check-new-files-necessary.ts to broaden the criteria for reading new files. The logic now triggers 'YES' if new files provide a better answer, rather than just if the request is different. This internal adjustment aims to improve context retrieval for complex queries.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal helper that decides when to look at additional files has gotten smarter. Before, it would only fetch new files if your new question seemed different from the last one; now, it will also do so if reading more files could give you a better answer, even for follow-up questions. This is an internal adjustment, so you probably won't notice anything different right away, but it should help the assistant give more thorough answers to complex or detailed requests.

ai.title: Remove spinner restart on chunk
ai.summary: Removes `Spinner.get().start()` call in `npm-app/src/cli.ts`. Prevents spinner restarting immediately after stopping during chunk processing.

eli5.text: The spinning loading indicator animation no longer restarts itself every time a new portion of text appears while you wait for a response. Previously, after briefly stopping to display each chunk of incoming content, it would immediately start spinning again; now it stays stopped during that chunk display so the text feels steadier as it streams in. This only affects how the waiting animation behaves behind the scenes and is already live today.

ai.title: Planning file selection switched to gemini2flash
ai.summary: getRelevantFilesForPlanning in backend/src/planning.ts switched from promptClaude to promptGemini using geminiModels.gemini2flash. system-prompt.ts raised getSearchSystemPrompt maxTokens from 200_000 to 500_000. Planning messages now route through messagesWithSystem helper. Backend planning subsystem only.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal file-picking step now uses a different, faster AI model to decide which files matter for a task, so the planning stage can handle bigger prompts without choking. Anyone relying on the planning backend benefits the moment this rolls out: larger requests that used to get cut short are now processed in full. If you watched the planning service right now, you'd see it quietly swap to the lighter model and accept prompts five times larger than before.

ai.title: Refine SEARCH/REPLACE prompt instructions for large files
ai.summary: Updated `generate-diffs-prompt.ts` and `process-file-block.ts` to enforce minimal SEARCH content and explicit whitespace/quote handling in AI prompts. The retry logic now logs detailed context (duration, snippets, file paths) when initial diff blocks fail to match. This aims to reduce matching errors in large files by guiding the model toward more precise, compact edit blocks.

eli5.text: When the system tries to edit a large file and the first attempt doesn't match the file correctly, it now gets clearer instructions to use shorter, more precise snippets and pay close attention to spaces, tabs, and quote marks. You would notice this only if you looked at the logs while editing large files: instead of generic retry messages, you'd see detailed records of what failed, including how long it took, which file was being edited, and the exact text that didn't match. This helps the system fix mistakes faster when it tries again.

ai.title: Planning reuses main processFileBlock
ai.summary: Refactors backend/src/planning.ts to remove local processFileBlock implementation and import shared version from backend/src/process-file-block.ts. Updates planComplexChange signature to accept WebSocket and pass it to shared processor. Aligns planning edit handling with main agent flow, eliminating duplicate lazy-edit logic.

eli5.text: When the system plans out edits to your files, it no longer uses a separate, duplicated set of editing logic. Instead, it now calls the same core file-editing routine that the main assistant already uses, so the way planned edits are handled matches the way direct edits are handled. You wouldn't notice a change in what gets edited, but the system is now using one consistent method behind the scenes, which removes redundant code and makes the behavior more predictable. This is live today and affects how the planning component processes file changes.

ai.title: System prompt adds markdown command block guidance
ai.summary: Added instruction to system prompt allowing agents to display terminal commands via markdown code blocks without execution. This clarifies how to present commands to users when actual execution is unnecessary or restricted. Change applies only to backend/src/system-prompt.ts.

eli5.text: When an assistant wants to show you a terminal command without running it, it can now display that command inside a formatted code block labeled as bash. Previously, the system had no clear option for showing commands as text only. This applies to the assistant's instructions for how it presents terminal commands to you.

ai.title: Homepage video layout fix
ai.summary: Homepage video layout stabilized. Outer `div` replaced with `section`, inner `div` switched to fixed `aspect-[13/9]`. Video element uses absolute positioning with `object-cover` to prevent layout shift.

eli5.text: The homepage video stopped jumping around as the page loaded. If you visit the homepage today, the video now stays in a fixed-size spot from the moment it appears instead of reshaping itself after loading. Behind the scenes, the video area keeps a steady width-to-height ratio and the video itself scales to fill that space neatly, so nothing shifts while everything settles into place.
